historical_growth.growth_rate_source: fcf_5yr_cagr - primary anchor reflecting cash-generative distribution business profile; EPS CAGR is distorted by the FY2024 Chemist Warehouse contract loss (~A$1.9B revenue) and elevated D&A/DC transition costs in FY2025-FY2026; equity CAGR inflated by M&A-driven goodwill and retained earnings; scenario growth rates further calibrated to FY2026 EBITDA guidance of A$610-620M and management's FY2027+ capex reduction (-30%) inflection
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (-1.4%) diverges materially from Equity 3yr CAGR (+12.6%), driven by the Chemist Warehouse wholesale contract loss in FY2024 (A$1.9B revenue) and the peak DC renewal program investment cycle (elevated D&A A$67M H1 FY2026 +21% YoY, capex A$136M FY2026 guided). FY2025 EPS of 109.7 AUD cents is a trough; management guides EPS recovery from FY2027 as D&A normalises and capex falls ~30%. Equity growth reflects book value accretion via acquisitions and retained earnings rather than current earnings power. FCF CAGR used as primary anchor with scenario assumptions calibrated to guided FY2026-FY2027 trajectory.

growth_rate_notes: Y1 (FY2026): -11% from FY2025 FCF base; reflects peak capex (A$136M guided), elevated DC transition costs (A$20M restructuring H1 FY2026), negative working capital H1 FY2026 (-A$24M FCF); full-year FCF estimated A$261M consistent with A$615M EBITDA guidance minus capex/interest/tax
Y2 (FY2027): +28% inflection; capex falls ~30% to ~A$95M, DC automation benefits flow through, EBITDA grows mid-single-digit to ~A$650M, interest costs stabilise
Y3 (FY2028): +10% sustained EBITDA growth, full DC automation leverage, MedTech and pharmacy network scale benefits
Y4 (FY2029): +8% continued organic growth across all segments
Y5 (FY2030): +6% decelerating toward terminal rate as scale normalises
base.wacc_notes: Risk-free rate 4.5% (10yr NZ govt bond) + equity risk premium 5.0% (ANZ market) + beta ~0.85 (healthcare distribution, defensive) + size/country premium 0.5% = approx 9.0%. EBOS is a regulated healthcare distributor with government-contracted revenues, justifying below-market beta.
base.terminal_growth_notes: Reflects long-run ANZ healthcare spending growth (aging demographics, PBS expenditure growth) offset by PBS price reform headwinds. Broadly in line with nominal ANZ GDP growth expectations. GLP-1 and specialty medicine structural tailwinds support upper end.

growth_rate_notes: Y1 (FY2026): -5% only modest FCF decline; fuel cost headwind partly offset by government cost recovery discussions and CSO expansion from July 2026, H2 FY2026 FCF strongly positive
Y2 (FY2027): +35% sharp inflection; capex -30%, Kemps Creek full-year automation running, GLP-1 volumes continue surging, MedTech 15%+ organic growth, pharmacy network SSS acceleration
Y3 (FY2028): +14% EBITDA margin expansion, all DC sites fully optimised, origin biologics US opportunity emerging
Y5 (FY2030): +8% premium growth sustained by diversified healthcare platform
bull.wacc_notes: Lower WACC reflects successful deleveraging to below 1.7x (within target range) and demonstrated operational resilience, reducing equity risk premium.
bull.terminal_growth_notes: Higher terminal growth reflects GLP-1 secular tailwind entrenching EBOS as critical high-value medicine infrastructure, plus MedTech and Animal Care above-market growth compounding into perpetuity.

growth_rate_notes: Y1 (FY2026): -18% severe FCF decline; additional customer contract losses, fuel costs not recovered, WC deteriorates further, EBITDA comes in at A$600M (misses downgraded guidance)
Y2 (FY2027): +10% partial recovery only; DC automation benefits delayed, interest costs remain elevated, leverage approaches upper target boundary
Y3-Y5: Low single-digit growth as competitive dynamics and margin pressure persist
bear.wacc_notes: Higher WACC reflects leverage remaining elevated (above 2.3x target ceiling), risk of covenant pressure, and equity risk premium expansion if guidance is missed again. Consistent with a market that has lost confidence in the DC program timeline.
bear.terminal_growth_notes: Conservative long-run growth assuming PBS price reforms accelerate and Animal Care premiumisation stalls.

valuation.currency_note: All monetary values in AUD millions except per-share intrinsic values which are shown in both AUD and NZD. NZD values use AUD/NZD rate of 1.10.

base.note: Entry price to achieve 15% CAGR to terminal value per share (NZD basis). Current NZD 20.65 is 16.6% above the 15% CAGR entry price, implying the stock is not yet at a 15%-CAGR buy point on the base DCF.

sensitivity.note: Matrix uses base case FCF growth rates [-11%, +28%, +10%, +8%, +6%] with varying WACC and terminal growth. Values in NZD per share at AUD/NZD 1.10.

sanity_check.tripped_on: Bear case EV/EBITDA (5.2x) is below the historical support level of approximately 7-8x, which represents distressed-company territory for a regulated healthcare distribution business. Base and bull cases passed.

current_market_multiples.note: Market is already at multi-year low multiples, reflecting the Chemist Warehouse contract loss (FY2024), peak DC investment cycle, and April 2026 guidance downgrade. EV/EBITDA 8.1x forward is the lowest in EBOS's recent history (FY2020: 11.7x, FY2021: 15.4x, FY2022: 18.5x, FY2023: 13.9x, FY2024: 9.8x).

base.assessment: REASONABLE - represents a very modest re-rating (+1.1x turn) from current depressed market multiple, consistent with market pricing in partial recovery

bull.assessment: REASONABLE - within EBOS historical range (FY2023 peak was 13.9x); requires DC automation to deliver as guided and GLP-1 tailwind to continue

bear.assessment: FLAGGED - below historical floor of 7-8x; represents a 'market loss of confidence' scenario where EBOS re-rates to pure logistics/infrastructure multiple, stripping out the regulated healthcare premium. Retained as a genuine stress scenario but acknowledged as extreme.

historical_ev_ebitda_range.comment: The historical 12-18x EV/EBITDA range reflected peak growth expectations in FY2021-FY2022. Post-Chemist Warehouse loss the market has structurally re-rated EBOS closer to 8-10x. Our base DCF at 9.2x is consistent with this new range.

sanity_check.auto_fix_notes: Bear case FCF growth rates were reviewed. Minimum Y1 change of -18% retained (vs original -20% considered) as it produces a plausible but severe outcome if working capital deteriorates and capex overruns. The 5.2x EV/EBITDA bear case is acknowledged as an extreme de-rating scenario and documented rather than mechanically floored. No base or bull case adjustments were required.
sanity_check.key_observation: The current NZD 20.65 price (EV/EBITDA 8.1x forward) is already pricing in substantial stress. Our base DCF at NZD 24.43 (9.2x forward EV/EBITDA) implies only modest undervaluation of 18%. The stock is not deeply cheap on a pure DCF basis but the risk/reward is skewed positively given: (1) the DC capex cycle is nearly complete, (2) management has guided FY2027 FCF inflection, (3) GLP-1 structural tailwind is durable, and (4) the business has government-contracted revenue protecting against catastrophic downside.

valuation_philosophy.primary_method: Discounted Free Cash Flow (5-year explicit period + perpetuity terminal value)
valuation_philosophy.fcf_definition: Reported free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditure) as per annual reports. H1 FY2026 FCF (-A$24M) is treated as suppressed by peak capex and working capital timing; FY2025 actual (A$293.4M) used as base.
valuation_philosophy.currency_handling: DCF performed entirely in AUD (reporting currency). Intrinsic value converted to NZD at AUD/NZD 1.10 for comparison to the NZX-listed share price. AUD/NZD rate sourced from cross-referencing dividend conversion rates disclosed in H1 FY2026 results.
valuation_philosophy.key_driver: The primary value driver is the FY2027 free cash flow inflection when (a) capex falls ~30% as the A$360M DC renewal program completes, and (b) EBITDA continues growing mid-single-digit organically. The DCF is essentially a bet on management's ability to execute the promised transition from a peak-investment year (FY2026) to a cash-generative phase (FY2027+).
limitations: FCF in H1 FY2026 was -A$24M due to working capital timing; annualised H1 figures are not appropriate as a base; FY2025 full-year actual used instead
AUD/NZD rate of 1.10 is an approximation; material NZD strengthening would reduce the NZD intrinsic value
Model does not independently value the TerryWhite Chemmart pharmacy network (782 stores), DC real estate, or medical technology intangibles - these could support a sum-of-parts premium
Bolt-on M&A (a consistent EBOS strategy) is not modelled in base projections; any value-accretive acquisitions are upside to the base case
